distinguishing_features: Couples a sacrificial anode array directly to the titanium anode bus to impose cathodic protection on the Ti surface
Uses the anolyte's high conductivity as the electrolytic path enabling close-contact (<1 cm) sacrificial protection
Sizes sacrificial anode current to match the Ti anodic current density (i_req = i_Ti × η_eff) rather than dosing an additive
Employs Mg-Zr / Zn-In rods physically decoupled from the anolyte pH driving force while shifting Ti potential into the immunity zone
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent corrosion/pitting of the titanium anode coating in high-conductivity, high-pH chloride anolyte by holding the Ti surface potential in the immune region rather than by chemical additive dosing or electrical telemetry inference.
parsed.viable_reason: Cathodically protecting a titanium anode with a sacrificial anode shorted to the same anode bus is self-defeating and physically implausible: a sacrificial Mg/Zn anode (E ≈ -1.6 to -1.0 V) shorted to the operating Ti anode would drive it anodically and be consumed at enormous current (≈1,000+ A/m²), so it would not shift Ti into an immunity zone and would be rapidly depleted.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art teaches galvanic/sacrificial cathodic protection of a working titanium anode via a bus-shorted anode array, so the proposed distinguishing mechanism is not a routine extension of the cited dosing or telemetry approaches.
